notes: Abstract only; no full text. The abstract names no eligibility rule for the 550 students. 'Tiered framework' and 'at-risk students' appear only in the motivation and closing sentences, not in the sample definition (tie-breaker 7), so unclear rather than targeted_low. Kraft lists n = 284 and grades 4-6, while the abstract reports n = 550 in grades 4-8, so Kraft's effect likely comes from a subsample; mixed_samples = 1. evidence_quote: All participating schools met the following criteria for inclusion in the project: (a) is an elementary school; (b) has been implementing positive behavioral interventions and supports (PBIS) for at least 1 year, as documented by district records
resolved_title: A Randomized Waitlist Controlled Analysis of Team-Initiated Problem Solving Professional Development and Use
notes: Full text read. Selection criteria are program-membership criteria (elementary school, PBIS user for one year, SWIS user, monthly team meetings); schools were recruited by letter and the first with documented interest were enrolled. No need or achievement rule at any level, so universal per tie-breaker 6. Kraft's math effects are school-level end-of-grade achievement for all K-5 students in the 38 schools (19 immediate, 19 waitlist). WWC sample text agrees: all K-5 schools implementing PBIS for at least one year, 59 percent free lunch reported as a description only.

evidence_quote: We first used data from the National Center for Education Statistics‘ Common Core of Data (CCD) 2004-2005 to identify all school districts in the United States with at least 570 teachers in elementary schools and 50 percent of students eligible for free or reduced-price meals under the federal government‘s National School Lunch Program.
resolved_title: Impacts of Comprehensive Teacher Induction: Results From the Second Year of a Randomized Controlled Study (NCEE 2009-4072)
notes: Long Mathematica/IES report; read executive summary and Chapter II. Districts were screened on size and poverty (50 percent NSLP eligibility), so the selection is on a non-achievement characteristic at the district level. Within districts, all eligible beginning teachers in nominated schools were included, and student test scores cover all students in tested grades with pre and post scores; no student rule. Executive summary restates the rule at p. xxiii (PDF p. 22). Report gives separate one-year (10 districts) and two-year (7 districts) results; Kraft's n = 3000 with reading and math effects of 0.00 and -0.01 in K-6 is consistent with the pooled or one-year student samples, and both sets share the same district rule, so mixed_samples = 0.
